## Task

## Trial `mariadb-galera-ubuntu16__FRdLcVu`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct, coherent state and transition evidence. The cluster was healthy, multi-primary replication worked through every member, and a bounded node3 outage demonstrated continued read/write service, automatic IST catch-up, and full recovery. Only minor temporary-file residue reduced operational hygiene.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.990 | 86/6 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node1, node2, and node3 form a healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
  - **Why:** All three members directly reported active and enabled MariaDB services, cluster size 3, Primary status, Connected, Synced, Ready, and the same three incoming member addresses. The same healthy state was observed after the disruption test.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e345f219a6ed480b`, `cmd-48ade3c6749d4b73`, `cmd-6bb2f61652b24868`, `cmd-240eef1a92834223`, `cmd-c8c6a658be444bf7`, `cmd-68d87f4a0d1445a1`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Writes made through any cluster member are available from the other members.
  - **Why:** Distinct rows were written through node1, node2, and node3. Subsequent reads on every member returned all three rows with the same wsrep commit position.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-665ee5a8d5db45ea`, `cmd-663fccdaa0a54ddc`, `cmd-3229bfb72f534085`, `cmd-11adc1728dac4115`, `cmd-176c5d08599a4a34`, `cmd-b6d1d4f9480340c7`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** The database remains readable and writable during one-member unavailability, and the returning member automatically rejoins with all writes made during its absence.
  - **Why:** After a healthy three-member baseline, node3 was stopped and directly shown to have no MariaDB process or database listeners. Node1 and node2 remained a two-member Primary, Synced, Ready component, served reads, and accepted mutually replicated writes. Node3 then started normally from stale sequence 5, automatically received two missing writesets through IST, reached sequence 7 in Synced/Ready state, and contained both outage-period rows. A post-rejoin write through node3 replicated to the other members, and all three finished at cluster size 3 with identical six-row data and commit position 8.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e345f219a6ed480b`, `cmd-48ade3c6749d4b73`, `cmd-6bb2f61652b24868`, `cmd-bf45e2f31d7b49e1`, `cmd-d7ba56bd57dc4cb4`, `cmd-5f33ae4ea9a4446c`, `cmd-b79d128cfa454558`, `cmd-fe89282279eb486d`, `cmd-9281391a1bf54027`, `cmd-dd8bd6aa39cf4045`, `cmd-320bd1b7c3054d33`, `cmd-7e5cda6bf51946f2`, `cmd-240eef1a92834223`, `cmd-c8c6a658be444bf7`, `cmd-68d87f4a0d1445a1`
